# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm docs:tools` from the registered tool definitions. Do not edit by hand. -->

The engineering bundle registers **132 tools** for L5X and Migration and Engineering resources and FactoryTalk View and MotionWorks IEC. Each tool answers with a summary,
structured data and suggested next calls; expected failures return a code, a message and a fix.
See [Examples](../examples.md) for end-to-end usage and the [README](../../README.md) for components and switches.

## L5X

### L5X read

Open a Studio 5000 L5X export and read its structure and components.

#### `open_project`

Open one Studio 5000 L5X export for this chat. Returns a project_id and a structure summary; every other tool reads this project.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Path to the .L5X export, absolute or relative to the workspace root. Example: "C:/Projects/Line/Line.L5X" |

#### `project_overview`

Structure and coverage of the open project: controller, revision, tasks, programs and component counts.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `list_components`

List one component kind in the open project, paginated. Use it to find the exact name get_component expects.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string (program \| task \| tag \| udt \| routine \| aoi \| module \| alarm) | yes | Component kind to list. |
| `scope` | string | no | Program name for a program-scoped tag or routine. Omit for controller scope. |
| `filter` | string | no | Case-insensitive substring matched against the component name. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Zero-based index of the first row to return. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum rows to return. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `get_component`

Read one component in full by exact name: a tag, UDT, routine, AOI, module, program, task or alarm.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string (program \| task \| tag \| udt \| routine \| aoi \| module \| alarm) | yes | Component kind to read. |
| `name` | string | yes | Exact component name as the export declares it. |
| `scope` | string | no | Program name when the component is program-scoped. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

### L5X references

Follow a symbol through exported logic without opening every routine.

#### `search_logic`

Find literal text in routine logic. Use it to locate a rung, ST line or operand when you do not know the exact symbol name; use find_references when you do.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Case-insensitive text to find, matched literally inside rung text, ST lines and diagram node labels. Example: "OTE(Motor_Run)". |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum matches to return. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `find_references`

Find where one symbol is read or written in exported logic, with scope, access and confidence. Use trace_dependencies for what feeds a symbol.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | string | yes | Symbol to follow, as declared or as written in logic. Example: "Motor_1" or "Program:MainProgram.Motor_1". |
| `scope` | string | no | Program scope to search. Omit to search every scope. |
| `detail` | string (summary \| evidence) | no | How much evidence to return. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum evidence rows when detail is "evidence". |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `trace_dependencies`

Follow what feeds a symbol (upstream) or what it feeds (downstream) through parsed operands. Static evidence only; it does not establish runtime causality.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | string | yes | Symbol to trace. Example: "Conveyor_Run" or "AOI_EncoderScale::Out_FPM". |
| `scope` | string | no | Program or AOI name that declares the symbol. Omit for controller scope; an AOI::Member symbol resolves against that AOI automatically. |
| `direction` | string (upstream \| downstream) | no | Which way to follow the graph. |
| `depth` | integer | no | Maximum graph depth to follow. Default 3. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `resolve_tag`

Resolve one Logix address against exported declarations: alias chain, member, integer bit and array subscript, with the evidence that remains unverified.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | yes | Address as written in logic. Example: "Motor_1.Speed" or "Alarms[2].3". |
| `scope` | string | no | Program scope for a local tag. Omit for controller scope. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `usage_map`

Map how one declared tag is used: which array elements and bits are read or written, which remain free, and where each appears.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tag` | string | yes | Declared tag name. Example: "Alarm_Bits". |
| `scope` | string | no | Declaring scope: "controller" or a program name. Defaults to controller. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

### L5X checks

Evidence-backed structural checks and export comparison.

#### `run_checks`

Run evidence-backed engineering checks on the open project: unused tags, unresolved references, unscheduled programs and undocumented logic, plus the standards rules a latch that nothing resets (LATCH_WITHOUT_RESET) and one output driven from two rungs (DUPLICATE_OUTPUT), and a rung written in an instruction spelling from the other revision (MNEMONIC_VERSION_MISMATCH), and the structure of every function block diagram (FBD_DANGLING_WIRE, OREF_DUPLICATE_DESTINATION, ICON_NO_MATCHING_OCON, FBD_FEEDBACK_CYCLE), and the rungs Studio refuses (RUNG_NO_OUTPUT, SBR_NOT_FIRST). Pass baseline_id to add I/O change checks against an earlier export.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline_id` | string | no | Optional second open project id to compare against, enabling I/O module change checks. |
| `rule` | string | no | Only return findings with this exact rule name. Example: "UNUSED_TAG". |
| `severity` | string (info \| warning \| critical) | no | Only return findings with this severity. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Zero-based index of the first finding to return. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum findings to return. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `compare_projects`

Compare two open exports by engineering component: programs, tasks, tags, UDTs, AOIs, modules, alarms, routines, rungs, ST bodies and diagrams. Export timestamps and XML formatting are ignored.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before_id` | string | yes | Project id of the earlier export. Open both exports first with open_project. |
| `after_id` | string | yes | Project id of the later export. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Zero-based index of the first change to return. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum changes to return. |

### L5X documentation

The instruction catalog the composer validates, and the handover bundle written to a new folder.

#### `list_instructions`

List the ladder instructions the composer validates: mnemonic, category, summary and operand slots with their kinds, plus the other published spelling when Logix Designer 36 renamed the instruction (also_published_as). Read it before composing a rung instead of guessing operand order.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string | no | Case-insensitive substring matched against the instruction name, category or summary. |
| `category` | string | no | Only instructions in this category, for example "Comparison". |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum rows to return. |

#### `document_project`

Write a documentation bundle for the open project into a NEW folder: project summary, I/O list, tag CSVs (including the Studio Tags and Comments shape) and per-program logic documentation — rungs with their comments and referenced tags, and the decoded elements of function block and sequential function chart routines. Never writes to the export.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `output_root` | string | yes | New folder for the bundle. It must not exist. Example: "C:/Projects/Line/documentation". |
| `include` | array | no | Optional parts to produce; default all. One of project, io, tags, rungs. |
| `programs` | array | no | Optional program names to restrict the bundle to. |
| `routines` | array | no | Optional routine names to restrict the rung documentation to. |
| `rungs_per_file` | integer | no | Most rungs per rung-documentation file before a continuation file is written. Defaults to 200. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

### L5X preview

Render proposed rungs as a viewer document so a chat answer shows ladder, not NeutralText.

#### `l5x_rung_preview`

Return proposed ladder rungs as paste-ready Studio neutral text, and write one minimal L5X preview document so the project viewer can show them. Validates every rung with the same parser draft_rung uses and refuses a rung that does not parse. The answer carries the exact block to paste into a ladder routine (`paste_text`); the diagram is drawn only when asked for. Nothing is imported and no project is modified.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rungs` | string | no | NeutralText rungs, one per line, for example "XIC(Start)OTE(Run);". Pass this or rungs_file. |
| `rungs_file` | string | no | Optional text file whose lines are the NeutralText rungs, one per line. Use it when the rungs are already written to disk. |
| `comments` | string | no | Optional rung comments, one per line, blank for a rung without a comment. |
| `title` | string | no | Optional document and controller name, for example "PumpStart". |
| `output` | string | no | Optional .L5X path to write, relative to the workspace. Defaults to ".l5x-preview/<title>.L5X". |
| `diagram` | string (yes \| no) | no | Draw the rungs as an SVG, plus a PNG when Chrome or Edge is installed. Defaults to no: the answer carries the paste-ready text, and a picture is only for review. |

#### `l5x_routine_diagram`

Draw a routine that already exists in the project as a ladder diagram, so an answer about live logic can show the rungs instead of NeutralText. Returns the SVG and, when Chrome or Edge is installed, a PNG. Reads the project; writes no project file and imports nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | no | Optional project handle. Omit when exactly one project is open. |
| `program` | string | yes | Program that owns the routine. Example: "MainProgram". |
| `routine` | string | yes | Routine to draw. Example: "MainRoutine". |
| `output` | string | no | Optional folder for the diagram, relative to the workspace. Defaults to ".l5x-preview". |
| `start_rung` | integer | no | Optional rung number to start drawing at, for a second page of a long routine. |
| `max_rungs` | integer | no | Most rungs to draw on one page. Defaults to 40. |

### L5X diagrams

Draw existing routines, or the whole project, as a schematic page.

#### `l5x_diagram`

Draw every ladder rung of the open project on one page as a schematic, so a review of unfamiliar logic can be answered with an image instead of NeutralText. Returns the SVG path and, when Chrome or Edge is installed, a PNG. Reads the project; writes only the image and imports nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | no | Optional project handle. Omit when exactly one project is open. |
| `program` | string | no | Optional program name to restrict the page to one program. |
| `routine` | string | no | Optional routine name to restrict the page to one routine. |
| `start_rung` | integer | no | Rung offset to start the page at, for reading a large project in pages. Defaults to 0. |
| `max_rungs` | integer | no | Most rungs to draw. Defaults to 60, at most 200. |
| `output` | string | no | Optional folder for the image, relative to the workspace. Defaults to ".l5x-diagram". |

### L5X drafts

Stage edits in a chat draft. `draft_apply` writes one new L5X beside the source and never overwrites it.

#### `draft_rung`

Append one ladder rung operation to the chat draft: replace, insert or delete. An insert puts the rung at the number it is given and renumbers the rungs below it, so a rung can go in at the top. The NeutralText is refused when it is malformed or when its right power rail is not driven by an output instruction, which Studio would reject at build time. Optionally carries the rung comment. Nothing is written until draft_apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `program` | string | yes | Program that owns the routine. Example: "MainProgram". |
| `routine` | string | yes | Routine the rung belongs to. Example: "MainRoutine". |
| `mode` | string (replace \| insert \| delete) | yes | replace rewrites an existing rung, insert adds one, delete removes one. |
| `rung` | integer | no | Rung number the operation targets. Required for replace and delete; for insert it is the position the new rung takes, 0..the current rung count. |
| `text` | string | no | NeutralText for replace or insert. Omit for delete. Example: "XIC(Start)OTE(Run);" |
| `before_rung` | integer | no | For insert only: put the new rung immediately before this rung; it must equal rung. |
| `comment` | string | no | Optional rung comment, written above the rung in Studio. Omit to leave an existing comment unchanged. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `draft_rung_comment`

Append one rung-comment change to the chat draft. Sets or clears the comment Studio shows above a rung; the logic is untouched. Nothing is written until draft_apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `program` | string | yes | Program that owns the routine. Example: "MainProgram". |
| `routine` | string | yes | Ladder routine the rung belongs to. Example: "MainRoutine". |
| `rung` | integer | yes | Rung number whose comment changes. |
| `comment` | string | yes | New comment text. Pass an empty string to clear an existing comment. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `compose_rung`

Compose one validated ladder rung from a structure or a named pattern, checking every instruction and operand against the export and against tags the same draft stages, and optionally stage it in the draft. Never emits text that fails the ladder parser or leaves the right power rail undriven.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | string (start_stop_latch \| fault_latch \| ton_delay \| interlock) | no | Named pattern to expand. fault_latch produces two rungs. |
| `spec_json` | string | no | Composition tree as JSON, for example {"series":[{"instr":"XIC","args":["Start"]},{"instr":"OTE","args":["Run"]}]}. |
| `arguments_json` | string | no | Pattern arguments as JSON, for example {"start":"Start","stop":"Stop","run":"Run"}. |
| `program` | string | no | Program to stage into. Omit to return the composed text only. |
| `routine` | string | no | Routine to stage into. Required with program. |
| `mode` | string (insert \| replace) | no | insert adds a rung; replace rewrites one. |
| `rung` | integer | no | Rung number for a staged operation. For a two-rung pattern, the second uses rung + 1. |
| `before_rung` | integer | no | For insert: insert before this rung number instead of after rung. |
| `comment` | string | no | Optional rung comment for the staged rung. |
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle to append to. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `compose_batch`

Compose and stage many validated ladder rungs in one call: every rung is checked against the export and against tags the same draft stages, and the whole batch is refused if any rung is invalid. Nothing is written until draft_apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rungs_json` | string | yes | Rungs as JSON, e.g. [{"spec":{"series":[{"instr":"XIC","args":["Start"]},{"instr":"OTE","args":["Run"]}]}},{"pattern":"ton_delay","arguments":{"tag":"Timer","seconds":5}}]. |
| `program` | string | yes | Program to stage into. Example: "MainProgram". |
| `routine` | string | yes | Routine to stage into. Example: "MainRoutine". |
| `rung` | integer | yes | First rung number for the batch; each later rung uses the next number. |
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle to append to. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `draft_st`

Append one Structured Text body replacement to the chat draft. Nothing is written until draft_apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `program` | string | yes | Program that owns the routine. Example: "MainProgram". |
| `routine` | string | yes | Structured Text routine to replace. Example: "Calc". |
| `code` | string | yes | Full replacement body, one statement per line. Example: "Counter := Counter + 1;\nIF Counter > 10 THEN Counter := 0; END_IF;" |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `draft_fbd`

Append one function block diagram sheet to the chat draft: blocks, references and wires. A block is an instance, so its tag must already be declared with the structure type Studio expects (FBD_MATH for ADD). Nothing is written until draft_apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `program` | string | yes | Program that owns the FBD routine. Example: "MainProgram". |
| `routine` | string | yes | Function block diagram routine to extend. Example: "LevelLoop". |
| `sheet` | integer | no | Sheet number to create. Defaults to 0. |
| `blocks` | string | yes | Blocks as JSON: [{"id":1,"type":"ADD","tag":"add1","structure":"FBD_MATH","pins":["SourceA","SourceB","Dest"]}]. |
| `refs` | string | no | References as JSON: [{"id":2,"direction":"in","tag":"Level"},{"id":3,"direction":"out","tag":"Flow"}]. |
| `wires` | string | no | Wires as JSON: [{"from":2,"to":1,"to_pin":"SourceA"},{"from":1,"to":3,"from_pin":"Dest"}]. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `draft_routine`

Append one new routine to the chat draft. Nothing is written until draft_apply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |

| `program` | string | yes | Program that will own the new routine. Example: "MainProgram". |

| `code` | string | yes | Body: NeutralText rungs for RLL, statements for ST. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

Throw away the staged draft, so edits that went the wrong way can be abandoned without writing a file. The project on disk is untouched.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle returned by a draft_* tool. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `draft_list`

List the staged operations of the draft with the index each one occupies, so a wrong edit can be removed without discarding the rest. Writes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle returned by a draft_* tool. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `draft_remove_op`

Remove exactly one staged operation from the draft, keeping the others. Call draft_list first: the index is positional, not a rung number.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | integer | yes | Zero-based index as draft_list reports it. |
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle returned by a draft_* tool. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `draft_validate`

Validate the accumulated draft against the open project and return its hash, diff summary and check findings. Writes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle returned by a draft_* tool. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `draft_apply`

Apply the validated draft to ONE new L5X file beside the source. Never overwrites, never imports into Studio, never contacts a controller.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle returned by a draft_* tool. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `output_path` | string | yes | New .L5X path to write. It must not exist. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

### L5X Studio SDK

Logix Designer SDK: export, verify, build and evidence review. Requires Studio 5000 and the SDK service.

#### `studio_sdk_status`

Preflight the Logix Designer SDK service, FactoryTalk Linx services, SDK package, .NET and installed Studio versions. Call before any SDK tool; no project or controller operation.

No parameters.

#### `studio_capabilities`

Report offline, SDK, revision-specific build, reference and live-read capabilities with next steps. Optional project_id checks the selected revision; no controller contact.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

#### `export_acd_to_l5x`

Export one existing offline ACD to a new full L5X with the running Logix Designer SDK service. No controller connection or upload; refuses to overwrite.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acd_path` | string | yes | Existing offline ACD. Example: "C:/Projects/Line/Line.ACD". |
| `output_path` | string | yes | New .L5X path to write. It must not exist. |

#### `verify_offline_l5x`

Import a full L5X into a new offline ACD and build it with the Studio SDK. The SDK opens a project with the Logix Designer release that matches the export revision, so that release must be installed — otherwise it answers STUDIO_VERSION_UNAVAILABLE and names the versions it has. A build then needs project revision 37+; probe=true attempts a lower revision and reports the SDK error. A safety controller is refused up front because the importer aborts it with XMLSrv_E_IMPORT_ABORTED_NO_CHANGES. No controller operation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |
| `baseline_id` | string | yes | Project handle of the unchanged baseline export this draft came from. Example: "3f2c...". |
| `output_path` | string | yes | New .ACD path to write. It must not exist. |
| `probe` | boolean | no | Attempt the build on a revision below 37 and report the SDK error instead of refusing early. |

#### `build_acd_from_draft`

Import one changed existing RLL or ST routine into a NEW offline ACD copy, build it, export it, and check preservation. No controller connection; requires the original ACD and a baseline exported in this chat.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acd_path` | string | yes | Original offline ACD the baseline was exported from. |
| `baseline_id` | string | yes | Project handle of the unchanged baseline export. |
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

Before reporting Studio findings, verify exact program, routine and rung or ST line names with verbatim quotes. Does not verify interpretation or runtime behavior.

|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |
| `citations` | string | yes | Citations to verify, one per line or as JSON. Example: "MainProgram/MainRoutine rung 4: XIC(Start)OTE(Run);" |

### L5X controller

Supervised controller access. Upload, mode changes and downloads require per-call human approval.

#### `controller_approval_status`

Read this session's permission preset and human-approval policy before upload, mode change or download. Full access normally cannot ask for approval. No SDK, file search or controller access.

No parameters.

#### `capture_controller_snapshot`

Upload from the supplied controller IP to a new local ACD. Resolve the exact FactoryTalk Linx route from a named ACD or L5X; requires per-call human approval.

| `ip_address` | string | yes | Controller IPv4 address the human named. Example: "192.168.1.10". |
| `route_project_path` | string | yes | ACD or L5X whose saved communications path names the controller route. Example: "C:/Projects/Line/Line.ACD". |
| `output_path` | string | yes | New .ACD path for the upload. It must not exist. |

#### `go_online`

Connect a matching ACD to a controller for read-only diagnostics. Does not change mode or controller data.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_path` | string | yes | ACD uploaded from that controller. Example: "C:/Projects/Line/Upload.ACD". |
| `ip_address` | string | yes | Controller IPv4 address. Example: "192.168.1.10". |

Read controller mode for the explicitly supplied controller IP. Supply the matching snapshot ACD to avoid reimporting an L5X. Read-only.

| `ip_address` | string | yes | Controller IPv4 address. Example: "192.168.1.10". |
| `snapshot_path` | string | no | Optional matching ACD upload. Omit to use the open project’s path for the route. |

#### `read_live_tag`

Read one controller-scoped scalar BOOL, INT, DINT or REAL from a matching uploaded ACD. Supply the declared data type; read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_path` | string | yes | ACD uploaded from that controller. |
| `ip_address` | string | yes | Controller IPv4 address. |
| `tag` | string | yes | Controller-scoped tag name. Example: "LineSpeed". |
| `data_type` | string (BOOL \| INT \| DINT \| REAL) | yes | Declared scalar type. |

#### `change_controller_mode`

Change controller mode to Program, Run or Test. Requires per-call human approval for the exact controller and target mode.

### L5X live

Direct EtherNet/IP reads with no Studio, FactoryTalk Linx or ACD snapshot.

#### `poll_live_tags`

Read declared scalar PLC tags directly over EtherNet/IP without Studio, FactoryTalk Linx, an ACD upload or the SDK. Explicit controller IPv4 and slot required. Returns timestamped sweeps, quality and controller identity; no writes.

| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

| `slot` | integer | no | CPU slot, 0 to 31. Default 0. |

| `sample_count` | integer | no | Number of sweeps to read. Default 1. |
| `interval_ms` | integer | no | Requested interval between sweeps. Default 200. |

#### `read_live_tags`

Read up to 64 declared scalar tags in ONE EtherNet/IP request (CIP tag group). Faster than polling for a one-shot snapshot; no writes, no Studio, no Linx, no SDK.

| `project_id` | string | no | Handle returned by open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open in this chat. |

| `slot` | integer | no | CPU slot, 0 to 31. Default 0. |
| `tags` | array | yes | Declared scalar tags to read together, 1 to 64. Each entry names the tag and optionally its program. |

#### `read_controller_clock`

Read controller identity and, on L8x controllers, the wall clock beside the workstation clock. Reports unsupported instead of guessing on other models. No writes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip_address` | string | yes | Controller IPv4 address the human named. Example: "192.168.1.10". |
| `slot` | integer | no | CPU slot, 0 to 31. Default 0. |

#### `discover_controllers`

Discover EtherNet/IP controllers on this LAN by UDP broadcast for a bounded window: address, product, revision, serial, status. No address needed, no writes, no Studio or Linx.

|---|---|---|---|
| `duration_seconds` | integer | no | How long to listen for replies, 1 to 15. Default 3. |

#### `write_live_tag`

Write ONE declared scalar PLC tag over EtherNet/IP, then read it back and report the controller's own value. Requires the row's writes switch AND human approval for this exact write. Destructive: it changes a running machine.

| `value` | value | yes | Value to write: true or false for BOOL, a number for INT, DINT or REAL. |

Set the controller wall clock (L8x only), then read it back. Requires the row's writes switch AND human approval for this exact change.

Start a bounded, read-only PLC trend as a session-owned background job. Explicit IPv4, slot and declared scalar tags required. SDK-independent EtherNet/IP; the chart follows the job without a model call per sample.

## Migration

### Migration

Assess a legacy RSLogix 500 export and lint the .L5K a migration wizard writes. Offline file readers; no controller and no claim that a file is migrated.

#### `migration_assess`

Assess one legacy export before a migration: for an .L5K it returns the lint verdict and the controller facts; for an RSLogix 500 .SLC text export it counts ladder files, rungs, racks and data files; for an .RSS, .ACH or .RSP container it states what the binary needs (RSLogix 500 or RSLogix 5, then Save As .SLC or the migration wizard). It never edits the file and never contacts a controller.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Path to the legacy file to assess (.l5k, .slc, .rss, .ach or .rsp). |

#### `l5k_lint`

Lint a Logix .L5K file before Studio imports it: report every import blocker (trailing comma in an attribute list, duplicate tag, name over 40 characters, stray routine parenthesis, unbalanced ROUTINE blocks) with its line number, plus what a text reader can count (tags, routines, rungs, modules, indirect addresses, controller revision). Reads UTF-16LE and UTF-8, because the migration wizard and a hand repair write different encodings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Path to the .L5K file, for example "PLC/Upgraded/SLITTER8_IMPORTED.l5k". |

#### `slc_read`

Read an RSLogix 500 .RSS/.ACH or RSLogix 5 .RSP project headlessly through its 32-bit automation server: program files with rung counts, the controller revision, optionally rung text, the symbol table and the data-file table. The project is opened hidden, read only and closed without saving, so no window appears and no click is needed. Requires RSLogix 500 or RSLogix 5 on the 32-bit host.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Absolute path to the legacy project, for example "RSS 500 Programs\Slitter8.RSS" or "RSS 5 Programs\EN-032.RSP". |
| `rungs` | integer | no | How many rung texts to include, 0 to 200. Defaults to 0 for counts only. |
| `symbols` | integer | no | How many symbol records to include, 0 to 5000. Defaults to 0 for the count only. |
| `data_files` | boolean | no | Include the data-file table (number, type, name, element count). Defaults to false. |

#### `migration_compare`

Compare an RSLogix 500 (.RSS, .ACH) or RSLogix 5 (.RSP) project read headlessly with the Logix .L5X export the migration produced: matched ladder files and routines, rung totals, symbol and data-file coverage, indirect addressing that survived, and every difference classified expected, real or cosmetic. Read-only; it does not claim runtime equivalence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | The legacy .RSS, .ACH or .RSP project. |
| `logix` | string | yes | The .L5X Studio exported after importing the migrated project. |

#### `migration_resolve`

Turn every PCE (program conversion error) marker and every unknown "?" operand the migration left in a Logix export into a work item: the legacy rung it came from, the instruction or operand the wizard could not carry, and a proposed Logix rewrite classified mechanical or review. Mechanical answers delete a marker whose rung already matches the legacy rung, fold a legacy timer/counter operand list into the timer or counter structure, or name the DINT tag a FOR loop needs; review answers a block transfer that became MSG, a rung that only cleared a status word, or a rung whose instructions no longer line up. Reads the legacy project headlessly and the .L5X; writes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | The legacy .RSS, .ACH or .RSP project the migration started from. |
| `logix` | string | yes | The .L5X Studio exported after importing the migrated project. |
| `routine` | string | no | Only report this routine, for example "_16_SPLICE". |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most work items to list. Defaults to 50. |

#### `migration_report`

Write the migration report a person reads before signing a conversion off: the two programs side by side, every PCE (program conversion error) marker and unknown "?" operand the wizard left with what it stands for, what a corrected export changed rung by rung, and the open items that need a human decision — a placeholder tag standing in for a module with no Logix equivalent (a 1747-SDN, say), a legacy I/O image kept as a plain tag array, an array indexed by a tag, sites still unanswered, legacy files with no counterpart, and a revision below the 37 an offline build needs. Writes a formatted Word document (.docx) or the same text as Markdown (.md), built from the legacy project, the wizard's .L5X and optionally the corrected .L5X; writes only the report.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | The legacy .RSS, .ACH or .RSP project the migration started from. |
| `logix` | string | yes | The .L5X Studio exported after importing the wizard's project. |
| `corrected` | string | no | The .L5X after the markers were answered, when one exists; the report then shows what changed. |
| `output` | string | yes | Path for the report: ".docx" for the Word document, ".md" for Markdown. Example: "migration-report.docx". |
| `title` | string | no | Heading to use instead of the controller type. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Rows per table before the rest are counted. Defaults to 20. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | Replace an existing report at that path. Defaults to false, so a report is never lost by accident. |

#### `migration_plan`

Record and read the resumable migration plan: the five decisions the intake interview must answer, the eight gated stages, the exceptions that remain and the evidence for each claim. Actions: create, read (default), answer, stage, exception. Writes only the plan JSON.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string (create \| read \| answer \| stage \| exception) | no | What to do with the plan. Defaults to read. |
| `path` | string | no | Plan path. Defaults to .migration/plan.json under the workspace. |
| `source` | string | no | For create: the legacy project path the plan is about. |
| `family` | string (slc500 \| plc5 \| unknown) | no | For create: which legacy family the source is. |
| `target_cpu` | string | no | Target Logix controller, for example 5069-L330ER. |
| `target_revision` | integer | no | Target firmware revision; 37 or newer can be proved by an offline build. |
| `io_strategy` | string | no | Keep the 1746 chassis behind a 1747-AENTR bridge, or replace the modules. |
| `hmi_scope` | string | no | Whether the HMI is in scope now or recorded for later. |
| `acceptance` | string | no | What proves the migration is accepted. |
| `stage` | string (intake \| assess \| convert \| lint \| import \| compare \| engineer \| commission) | no | For stage: which stage to set. |
| `status` | string (pending \| active \| done \| blocked) | no | For stage: the state to record. Defaults to done. |
| `evidence` | string | no | For stage: one line of evidence per entry, newline separated. |
| `note` | string | no | For stage: a short note that survives with the stage. |
| `id` | string | no | For exception: a stable id, for example "indirect-N7-130". |
| `kind` | string | no | For exception: what class of difference it is. |
| `description` | string | no | For exception: the difference in one sentence. |
| `rationale` | string | no | For exception: why it is accepted or how it was fixed. |
| `exception_status` | string (open \| accepted \| fixed) | no | For exception: its state. Defaults to open. |


## Engineering resources

### Engineering resources

The local standards corpus and the house-style profile read from the open project. No network, no model calls.

#### `engineering_reference`

Read the local engineering corpus: return the contents with no arguments, ranked pages for a query, or one page in full for an id. Pages carry rule IDs (CRAFT-NAME-01, VIEW-HPM-02, …) and their basis; nothing is fetched from the network.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | no | Topic, rule id or tag to search for, for example "state machine", "VIEW-HPM-02" or "seal-in". |
| `id` | string | no | Exact page id from the contents, for example "iec-state-machines". |
| `domain` | string | no | Optional domain filter: iec, rockwell, yaskawa, view, optix or craft. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most search hits to return; defaults to 8, maximum 20. |

#### `engineering_profile`

Read the house style of the open project: naming, logic idioms, HMI palette and fonts, comment density, with the evidence and a confidence level. Call it before authoring so new code follows the plant’s own conventions.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | no | L5X project handle from open_project. Omit when exactly one project is open. |
| `view_id` | string | no | FactoryTalk View handle from ftview_open. Provide this or project_id. |

### FTView read

| `root` | string | yes | Export folder containing the display XML files and the HMI tag CSV. Example: "C:/Projects/Line/ME Export". |

| `view_id` | string | no | View handle returned by ftview_open. Omit when exactly one export is open in this chat. |

Read one display or one HMI tag in full: a display exposes its named objects; a tag exposes its CSV row.

Join the HMI tags of one opened export to the tags and logic of a Studio 5000 L5X: device address to PLC tag, display usage, logic usage, and the tags that exist on only one side.

Run structural checks over one opened export: tag CSV integrity, duplicate names within displays and the tag file, files that did not parse, screens whose connection names a tag the CSV does not declare (TAG_NOT_BOUND), artwork a display names but the export does not ship (IMAGE_MISSING), and the alarm setup — a display-name that is missing from the export, a trigger with no message, a placeholder label, a trigger whose tag the HMI database lacks — read from Alarms/Alarms.xml or Alarms.xml when `alarms` is omitted. `coverage` names every check that did not run, such as tag binding on an export that carries no tag CSV. Vendor XSD validation and controller binding are not performed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Alarms.xml path, or a folder that contains it (an export, or <project store>\<application>). |
| `tags` | string | no | Optional HMI tag CSV for the same application; every trigger watching a tag it does not define is reported as unresolved. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most triggers and messages to list. Defaults to 50, at most 200. |

#### `ftview_studio_import_prepare`

Package displays from an applied export for Studioâ€™s Graphics Import Export Wizard: copies the selected <gfx> display XML files and writes the gfxImport batch file, then returns the wizard steps. Does not import by itself.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `export_root` | string | yes | Applied export folder that contains Displays/. |
| `displays` | string | yes | Display names to import, separated by commas, without .xml. |
| `output_root` | string | no | Optional new folder for the package; defaults to a folder under the system temp directory. |
| `mode` | string (create \| update) | no | Import mode: create new displays, or update existing ones. |
| `current_export` | string | no | Optional export of the application as it stands now; each display it already holds is written as an update instead of a create, so one batch cannot fail on a display that exists. |
| `skip_unchanged` | string (no \| yes) | no | With current_export: leave out displays whose objects already match the application, so the import only touches what changed. |

#### `ftview_capabilities`

Report what this host can do with FactoryTalk View: Studio and tag-wizard presence, installed Gfx schema versions, application count, and which steps need a running Studio. Read-only.

No parameters.

#### `ftview_apps`

List the FactoryTalk View ME applications installed on this host, through the vendor export server. Requires FactoryTalk View ME on the machine.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string | no | Case-insensitive substring matched against the application name. |

#### `ftview_export`

Export one installed ME application (displays and global objects) to a NEW folder through the vendor export server. If the project store holds a user-exported Alarms.xml or tag CSV, copy it as a snapshot and report its age and whether it is fresh, stale or missing; such files are not part of a normal application. When an asset is stale or missing the result points at ftview_studio_export_prepare and ftview_studio_export_accept. The application is not modified.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |

| `application` | string | yes | Application name as ftview_apps lists it. |
| `output_root` | string | yes | New folder for the export. It must not exist. |

#### `ftview_verify_import`

Compare the staged draft object by object with a fresh export of the application, proving whether the import landed. Exports through the vendor engine by default, or reads an export folder you made by hand (`export_root`), which is the only path when the vendor export is unavailable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view_id` | string | no | View handle returned by ftview_open. Omit when exactly one export is open in this chat. |
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle returned by an ftview_draft_* tool. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `application` | string | yes | Application name as ftview_apps lists it. The same application the package was imported into. |
| `export_root` | string | no | Export folder to verify against instead of running the vendor export, for a File > Export you made by hand after importing the package. |

#### `ftview_apply`

Write the prepared edits to a NEW export folder: changed files get the edits, other text exports are copied verbatim. The source folder is never modified.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | no | Draft handle returned by an ftview_draft_* tool. Omit when exactly one draft exists in this chat. |
| `output_root` | string | yes | Folder for the edited export. It must not exist unless overwrite is yes and this chat wrote it. Example: "C:/Projects/Line/ME Export Edited". |
| `overwrite` | string (no \| yes) | no | Re-write a folder this chat already applied into, instead of naming a new one. |
| `package` | string (delta \| full) | no | What the import manifest should list: only the displays this draft changed (delta) or every display in the export (full), which is what a fresh application needs. |

#### `ftview_render`

Draw one display, or up to eight in one call, of the open export as SVG files and as PNGs when a headless Chrome or Edge is installed, so the screens can be inspected before anyone imports them. Reports every object that leaves the canvas or overflows its box. Geometry and colour only: artwork is inlined when the export carries its file; animations and vendor widgets are drawn as labelled placeholders.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view_id` | string | no | View handle returned by ftview_open. Omit when exactly one export is open in this chat. |
| `display` | string | no | Display name as listed by ftview_list. Omit when displays_json is given. |
| `displays_json` | string | no | JSON array of up to 8 display names to draw in one call. Example: ["Main","Alarms"]. |
| `output` | string | no | Folder for the render. Defaults to a "renders" folder beside the export. |
| `source` | string (export \| draft) | no | Draw the committed export file or the staged draft that has not been applied yet. |
| `sheet` | string (no \| yes) | no | Stack every drawing on one review image with a title per display, so a set can be judged in a single look. |

### FTView Studio

Plan the manual FactoryTalk View Studio import for changed displays.

#### `ftview_studio_status`

Discover installed FactoryTalk View ME tooling: product folders, ME XSD schemas, help files and the Add Component utility. Read-only; does not start Studio or prove licensing.

No parameters.

#### `ftview_studio_preflight`

Check the files that differ between two opened exports for a manual Studio import: parse state, name restrictions, discovered utility and schemas, plus the engineering gate (critical check findings and house-theme conformance). Writes nothing and starts no Studio.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before_id` | string | yes | View id of the export before the edit. |
| `after_id` | string | yes | View id of the edited export. |
| `gate` | string (report \| fail) | no | report asks the gate to report its verdict; fail refuses when a critical finding or a non-conforming display remains. |

#### `ftview_studio_handoff`

Return the ordered manual FactoryTalk View Studio import plan for the changed displays between two opened exports. No vendor utility runs and no file is written.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before_id` | string | yes | View id of the export before the edit. |
| `after_id` | string | yes | View id of the edited export. |
| `application` | string | yes | ME application name the human opens in Studio. Example: "Line". |


## MotionWorks IEC

### MWI session

Find and stage a workspace project, then start, inspect and close the IDE.

#### `mw_project_find`

Find MotionWorks IEC projects inside the calling workspace. Returns each .mwt, its expanded directory, whether a staged copy exists and whether a pre-edit backup exists. Call this before opening anything.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filter` | string | no | Optional case-insensitive substring matched against the project name or path. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most projects to return. Defaults to 20. |

#### `mw_ide_status`

Report whether MotionWorks IEC is running, which project is open, the automation version, the active view, the compile state and any blocking dialog. Call it before and after operations that change the IDE.

No parameters.

#### `mw_project_stage`

Optional sandbox: copy one workspace project into .motionworks/stage so the IDE opens a copy instead of the real files. Normal editing opens the workspace project directly.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | Workspace project folder or its .mwt. Must be inside the workspace. |
| `replace_existing` | boolean | no | Replace an existing stage after review; defaults false. The previous stage is retained under backups/. |

#### `mw_project_open`

Open a workspace project directly, or a staged copy. A direct open first writes and verifies one complete backup under <workspace>/.motionworks/attached/, and a project the IDE already has open is attached without being reloaded. Refuses to replace another open project without the exact approved path.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Workspace .mwt (edits the real project, backup taken first) or a staged .mwt from mw_project_stage. |
| `user_approved` | boolean | no | True only after the user approved saving and closing another open project. |
| `expected_project` | string | no | Exact open project path named in that approval. |

#### `mw_ide_start`

Start MotionWorks IEC with one workspace project (backup first) or a staged copy, or attach to the IDE that is already running. Refuses when several projects are openable without a project argument.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | no | Workspace or staged .mwt to start with. Omit when exactly one project is openable. |

#### `mw_worksheet_open`

Open one code or variable worksheet, or resource globals, in the open staged project and verify the active view. Read-only: no edit, save, compile or download.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string (code \| variables) | yes | Worksheet kind: code or variables. |
| `pou` | string | no | POU name for a code worksheet. Omit for globals. |
| `inspect_only` | boolean | no | Check the current editor instead of opening one; defaults false. |

#### `mw_project_close`

Close MotionWorks IEC, saving the open project, after explicit user approval for that exact project.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user_approved` | boolean | yes | True only after the user approved saving and closing MotionWorks. |
| `expected_project` | string | no | Exact open project path named in the approval. |

### MWI read

Read the saved project model, code, references, review evidence and installed help.

#### `mw_project_overview`

Summarize one project from its saved files: languages, POU, variable, type and task counts, readiness and validation findings. Use it before listing components.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | no | Project directory or .mwt inside the workspace. Omit to use the single staged project. |

#### `mw_list`

List POUs, variables, globals, types, tasks or library blocks from the saved project, with a filter and paging.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string (pou \| variable \| global \| type \| task \| library) | yes | What to list. |
| `project` | string | no | Project directory or .mwt inside the workspace. Omit to use the single staged project. |
| `pou` | string | no | POU whose declarations to list; required for kind variable. |
| `filter` | string | no | Case-insensitive substring over the returned fields. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Rows to skip. Defaults to 0. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most rows. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. |

#### `mw_get`

Read one POU with its declarations and the text_body_sha256 that the edit preconditions take, one type, one task row, one block interface or the EtherNet/IP assembly map.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string (pou \| type \| task \| block \| eip) | yes | What to read. |
| `name` | string | no | Exact component name; omit only for kind eip. |
| `project` | string | no | Project directory or .mwt inside the workspace. Omit to use the single staged project. |
| `library` | string | no | Library name for a block interface. |

#### `mw_search`

Find literal text across the saved POU bodies, case-insensitively, with the POU and line of each match.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Literal text to find. |
| `project` | string | no | Project directory or .mwt inside the workspace. Omit to use the single staged project. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most matches. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. |

#### `mw_references`

Find where one symbol appears across the saved POU bodies, with the POU and line. Static evidence only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | string | yes | Declared or written symbol name. |
| `project` | string | no | Project directory or .mwt inside the workspace. Omit to use the single staged project. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most matches. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. |

#### `mw_review`

Run the static review: workflow readiness, native validation, unsupported constructs, and optionally a program review for one POU or proposed body.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | no | Project directory or .mwt inside the workspace. Omit to use the single staged project. |
| `pou` | string | no | POU to review. |
| `body` | string | no | Proposed replacement body to review without writing it. |

#### `mw_help`

Search installed MotionWorks help, the installed manuals, reviewed Yaskawa references or the versioned ST patterns.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string (help \| manual \| reference \| pattern) | yes | Where to search. |
| `query` | string | no | Search term or pattern name; omit to list what is available. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most rows. Defaults to 10, maximum 50. |
| `project` | string | no | Project directory or .mwt inside the workspace. Omit to use the single staged project. |

### MWI verify

Compile, read the IDE output panes and compare saved-source baselines.

#### `mw_compile`

Run Make (link changed sources), Build (full compile), or read the compile state of the open staged project. A verdict is the vendor engine's, not proof of runtime behavior.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string (make \| build \| state) | no | Compile operation: make, build or state. |

#### `mw_diagnostics`

Read one IDE output pane (Errors, Warnings or Build) as text, with the compile state attached. The API returns a verdict but not the messages, so this is the only source for exact text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pane` | string | no | Output pane name. Defaults to Errors. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Most messages. Defaults to 200, maximum 500. |

#### `mw_verify`

Capture a baseline of the saved project source and compile state, or compare the open project against a captured baseline. Reports added, removed and changed source files.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string (baseline \| compare) | no | Capture a baseline or compare against one. |
| `baseline_id` | string | no | Baseline id returned by a capture. Required when mode is compare. |

### MWI edit

On by default. Code, declarations, structure, block insertion and POU packages, each verified against saved and native state.

#### `mw_edit_code`

Replace one ST or IL body in the open project through the native ChangeCodeWS path. Supply exact find/replace changes with the body hash, or a complete body with the current body. Verifies saved and native state, then leaves compilation to mw_compile.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pou` | string | yes | Exact POU name. |
| `changes` | array | no | Exact find/replace changes; each must match its expected count. |
| `expected_body_sha256` | string | no | Exact 64-character text_body_sha256 from mw_get for kind pou, when using changes. |
| `body` | string | no | Complete replacement body, when not using changes. |
| `expected_body` | string | no | Current body that the complete replacement expects, when using body. |

#### `mw_edit_variables`

Add, edit or delete one declaration in the open project through the native IDE API. Edit replaces the complete seven-field declaration and optional boolean flags; delete needs approval and reference review.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operation` | string (add \| edit \| delete) | yes | Variable operation. |
| `pou` | string | no | POU for a local declaration; omit for resource globals. |
| `name` | string | no | Existing exact name for edit or delete. |
| `declaration` | object | no | Complete replacement declaration. |
| `flags` | object | no | Explicit boolean native variable flags; omitted flags stay unchanged. |
| `user_approved` | boolean | no | Approval for a deletion. |
| `references_reviewed` | boolean | no | Set after reviewing code and external references. |
| `rename_reviewed` | boolean | no | Set after reviewing references for a rename. |

#### `mw_edit_structure`

Create, copy, rename, delete, convert or assign one POU, or create, edit, delete, assign or unassign one task, through the native IDE API. Deletion and unassignment need approval; rename needs reference review.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | string (pou \| task) | yes | Structure kind. |
| `operation` | string (create \| copy \| rename \| delete \| edit \| assign \| unassign) | yes | Operation. |
| `name` | string | yes | Existing name for edit/delete/assign, or the new name for create. |
| `new_name` | string | no | New name for copy or rename. |
| `language` | string (ST \| IL \| FBD \| LD) | no | POU language for creation. |
| `pou_type` | string (PROGRAM \| FUNCTION_BLOCK \| FUNCTION) | no | POU type for creation. |
| `return_type` | string | no | Function return type. |
| `kind` | string (CYCLIC \| DEFAULT \| SYSTEM) | no | Task kind for creation. |
| `pou` | string | no | Program to assign to a task. |
| `instance` | string | no | Instance name for assign or unassign. |
| `settings` | object | no | Task settings to change; each value is a string. |
| `user_approved` | boolean | no | Approval for deletion or unassignment. |
| `references_reviewed` | boolean | no | Set after reviewing references for rename or delete. |

#### `mw_insert_block`

Insert one FB instance declaration and its ST call into a POU through the native APIs. Bindings are pin/value pairs; outputs and in-outs need existing direct variables. Requires the exact current body hash.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pou` | string | yes | Target ST POU. |
| `block` | string | yes | Function-block name to instantiate. |
| `instance` | string | yes | New instance name. |
| `bindings` | array | yes | Pin bindings; every in-out pin must be present. |
| `expected_body_sha256` | string | no | Exact 64-character hash of the current POU body, or use expected_body. |
| `expected_body` | string | no | Current POU body, or use expected_body_sha256. |
| `library` | string | no | Library that resolves a duplicate block name. |
| `group` | string | no | Declaration group for the instance; defaults to Default. |
| `before` | string | no | Unique exact text to insert before; mutually exclusive with offset. |
| `offset` | integer | no | Zero-based character offset at a line boundary; defaults to append. |

#### `mw_transfer_pou`

Export one writable POU to a private workspace package, or import that untouched package into this project. Import needs the export token and a dependency review; a token is consumed by one attempt.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `operation` | string (export \| import) | yes | Package operation. |
| `pou` | string | no | Exact POU to export. |
| `package_token` | string | no | Token returned by the export. |
| `dependencies_reviewed` | boolean | no | Set after reviewing the package externals before import. |

#### `mw_validate`

Validate the open project before applying: workflow blockers, native validation and an optional program review for one POU or proposed body. Read the findings before saving or compiling.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pou` | string | no | POU to review. |
| `body` | string | no | Proposed replacement body to review without writing it. |

#### `mw_apply`

Save the open project through the IDE. A workspace project is written in place; its verified pre-edit backup stays under <workspace>/backups/.

No parameters.
